Edges 1, 3, and 5 have an attribute w and are in the accent color; edges 2 and 4 have no w and are faded. The card maps edge id to value for the three edges that have it: 1 is 2, 3 is 5, 5 is 1." width="100%"} Reads one named attribute from many edges at once and returns it as a dictionary keyed by edge ID. By default every edge is examined; `sources=` and `targets=` narrow this down to edges with particular endpoints. Edges that don't have the attribute are left out of the result rather than mapped to `None`. The graph is not modified. This is the companion of `set_edge_attrs()` and is useful for: - collecting edge weights or other numeric edge data for further analysis - inspecting the relationship types (or other labels) on edges leaving or entering particular nodes - checking which edges carry a given attribute at all The name `"weight"` reads the edge's first-class weight; unweighted edges have no weight and are omitted. To look up edges by ID instead of by endpoints, use `get_edge_attrs_by_id()`; for a tabular view of all edge attributes, use `get_edge_df()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edge_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The name of the attribute to read (e.g., `"weight"`, `"rel"`). Edges without this attribute are omitted; if no edge has it, an empty dict is returned. [sources]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A list of node IDs or labels; only edges leaving one of these nodes are examined. If `None` (the default), the source is unrestricted. When combined with `targets=`, an edge must satisfy both filters. An unknown node raises a `ValueError`. [targets]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A list of node IDs or labels; only edges entering one of these nodes are examined. If `None` (the default), the target is unrestricted. For undirected graphs, an edge matches the `sources=`/`targets=` filters in either orientation. An unknown node raises a `ValueError`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, any]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping edge IDs (integers) to attribute values. Only includes edges that have the attribute set (and that pass the `sources=`/`targets=` filters). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node given in `sources=` or `targets=` does not exist in the graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Without filters, every edge that has the attribute is returned. Here all three edges are weighted, so all three edge IDs appear: ::: {#81d56951 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges( [ ("A", "B", 1.5, {"type": "friend"}), ("B", "C", 2.0, {"type": "colleague"}), ("C", "D", 1.0, {"type": "friend"}), ] ) ) graph.get_edge_attrs("weight") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {1: 1.5, 2: 2.0, 3: 1.0} ``` ::: ::: Any attribute name works the same way, including custom ones like `type`: ::: {#d84b49a2 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_edge_attrs("type") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {1: 'friend', 2: 'colleague', 3: 'friend'} ``` ::: ::: `sources=` restricts the lookup to edges leaving the given nodes. Only edge `2` (`B->C`) leaves `B`; the edge entering `B` from `A` is not included: ::: {#8c4813dc .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_edge_attrs("type", sources=["B"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {2: 'colleague'} ``` ::: ::: Combining `sources=` and `targets=` picks out edges between two groups of nodes: ::: {#157b5b0c .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_edge_attrs("weight", sources=["A", "C"], targets=["B", "D"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` {1: 1.5, 3: 1.0} ``` ::: :::
